paperInfo.subject: Science and Technology
paperInfo.sourceNote: Original expanded structured practice questions informed by ZIMSEC Grade 7 Science and Technology structure and publicly available revision/specimen material; not verbatim past-paper reproduction.

questions.questionText: Explain two characteristics that show that an organism is living. Give one example of a living organism.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Living things grow, respire, reproduce, feed, excrete, respond to stimuli or move. Any two correctly explained characteristics earn credit.
questions.explanation: A characteristic is accepted when it is stated and appropriately explained.

questions.questionText: Describe the functions of the root, stem and leaf in a flowering plant.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water/mineral salts; the stem supports the plant and transports materials; leaves make food by photosynthesis and exchange gases.
questions.explanation: Functions should be matched to the correct plant parts.

questions.questionText: State two conditions necessary for successful seed germination and explain why each is needed.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Water is needed to activate processes and soften the seed coat; oxygen is needed for respiration; suitable warmth supports enzyme activity.
questions.explanation: Any two correct conditions with explanations are acceptable.

questions.questionText: Construct a simple four-organism food chain using a green plant, a herbivore, a carnivore and a decomposer. Explain the direction of energy flow.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Example: grass → grasshopper → frog → decomposer. Energy originates from the Sun, is captured by plants and passed through feeding relationships.
questions.explanation: Arrows should show feeding/energy transfer in the correct direction.

questions.questionText: Describe evaporation, condensation and precipitation as stages of the water cycle.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Evaporation changes liquid water to vapour; condensation changes vapour into tiny liquid droplets; precipitation returns water to Earth as rain or other forms.
questions.explanation: Each stage must be correctly described.

questions.questionText: Explain the main role of the respiratory system and describe how oxygen reaches the blood.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: The respiratory system brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide. In the lungs, oxygen passes from air spaces into the blood by gas exchange.
questions.explanation: The answer should link breathing, lungs and gas exchange.

questions.questionText: Give three ways of preventing the spread of infectious diseases in a community and explain each.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Handwashing removes microbes; safe water and sanitation reduce contamination; vaccination can protect against specific diseases; covering coughs limits droplets.
questions.explanation: Any three appropriate measures with explanations.

questions.questionText: Describe how to make a simple electric circuit using a cell, wires, a switch and a bulb. Explain what happens when the switch is opened.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Connect the cell, wires, switch and bulb to form a closed loop. Closing the switch completes the circuit and the bulb lights; opening it breaks the circuit and the bulb goes off.
questions.explanation: The key idea is a complete conducting path.

questions.questionText: Explain friction and give two useful examples and one disadvantage of friction.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Friction is a force opposing motion between surfaces. It helps walking and braking, but can cause wear and heat in moving machine parts.
questions.explanation: Examples must clearly relate to friction.

questions.questionText: Name four weather instruments and state what each measures.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Thermometer—temperature; rain gauge—rainfall; wind vane—wind direction; anemometer—wind speed; barometer—air pressure.
questions.explanation: Accept four correctly matched instruments and measurements.

questions.questionText: Compare renewable and non-renewable energy sources. Give two examples of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Renewable sources are replenished naturally, e.g. solar and wind. Non-renewable sources are finite, e.g. coal and petroleum.
questions.explanation: The comparison must distinguish replenishment/finite supply.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials and give one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Transparent materials transmit most light, translucent materials transmit some light, and opaque materials block light. Examples: clear glass, frosted glass, wood.
questions.explanation: Definitions and examples should match.

questions.questionText: Explain how sound is produced and how it travels from a vibrating source to a listener.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: A vibrating source makes surrounding particles vibrate, producing sound waves that travel through a medium to the listener's ear.
questions.explanation: The response should mention vibration and a medium.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between input and output devices and give three examples of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Input devices send data to a computer, e.g. keyboard, mouse and microphone. Output devices present processed information, e.g. monitor, printer and speakers.
questions.explanation: Examples must be correctly classified.

questions.questionText: State four safe practices when using the internet and explain why each is important.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Use strong passwords, avoid sharing private information, do not open suspicious links, use trusted sites/software and report harmful behaviour. These reduce fraud, malware and privacy risks.
questions.explanation: Any four well-explained practices.

questions.questionText: Explain how a spreadsheet can be used to calculate the total cost of items purchased. Include a suitable formula example.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Enter item prices in cells and use a SUM formula such as =SUM(B2:B6) to add them. A spreadsheet reduces manual calculation errors and allows easy changes.
questions.explanation: Formula and purpose should be clear.

questions.questionText: Explain why soil is important to crop production and describe two ways of maintaining soil fertility.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Soil provides support, water and mineral nutrients. Fertility can be maintained through crop rotation, adding organic manure/compost, appropriate fertilisers and erosion control.
questions.explanation: Any two appropriate methods with explanation.

questions.questionText: Describe two methods of controlling crop pests and state one advantage of integrated pest management.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Methods include biological control, cultural practices, mechanical removal and appropriate pesticides. Integrated management combines suitable methods and can reduce over-reliance on chemicals.
questions.explanation: Methods and advantage should be correctly related.

questions.questionText: Explain the importance of keeping farm records. Name three records a farmer may keep.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Records help monitor production, costs, sales and profit and support planning. Examples include sales records, input records, livestock records and cash records.
questions.explanation: Any three valid record types.

questions.questionText: Describe three ways people can reduce environmental pollution in their community.
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Proper waste disposal, recycling/reuse, treatment of sewage, reducing smoke emissions and planting trees can reduce pollution.
questions.explanation: Any three suitable measures with explanation.

questions.explanation: The key idea is a complete conducting path.

questions.questionText: Explain friction and give two useful examples and one disadvantage of friction. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 89)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Friction is a force opposing motion between surfaces. It helps walking and braking, but can cause wear and heat in moving machine parts.
questions.explanation: Examples must clearly relate to friction.

questions.questionText: Name four weather instruments and state what each measures. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 90)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Thermometer—temperature; rain gauge—rainfall; wind vane—wind direction; anemometer—wind speed; barometer—air pressure.
questions.explanation: Accept four correctly matched instruments and measurements.

questions.questionText: Compare renewable and non-renewable energy sources. Give two examples of each. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 91)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Renewable sources are replenished naturally, e.g. solar and wind. Non-renewable sources are finite, e.g. coal and petroleum.
questions.explanation: The comparison must distinguish replenishment/finite supply.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials and give one example of each. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 92)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Transparent materials transmit most light, translucent materials transmit some light, and opaque materials block light. Examples: clear glass, frosted glass, wood.
questions.explanation: Definitions and examples should match.

questions.questionText: Explain how sound is produced and how it travels from a vibrating source to a listener. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 93)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: A vibrating source makes surrounding particles vibrate, producing sound waves that travel through a medium to the listener's ear.
questions.explanation: The response should mention vibration and a medium.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between input and output devices and give three examples of each. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 94)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Input devices send data to a computer, e.g. keyboard, mouse and microphone. Output devices present processed information, e.g. monitor, printer and speakers.
questions.explanation: Examples must be correctly classified.

questions.questionText: State four safe practices when using the internet and explain why each is important. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 95)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Use strong passwords, avoid sharing private information, do not open suspicious links, use trusted sites/software and report harmful behaviour. These reduce fraud, malware and privacy risks.
questions.explanation: Any four well-explained practices.

questions.questionText: Explain how a spreadsheet can be used to calculate the total cost of items purchased. Include a suitable formula example. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 96)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Enter item prices in cells and use a SUM formula such as =SUM(B2:B6) to add them. A spreadsheet reduces manual calculation errors and allows easy changes.
questions.explanation: Formula and purpose should be clear.

questions.questionText: Explain why soil is important to crop production and describe two ways of maintaining soil fertility. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 97)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Soil provides support, water and mineral nutrients. Fertility can be maintained through crop rotation, adding organic manure/compost, appropriate fertilisers and erosion control.
questions.explanation: Any two appropriate methods with explanation.

questions.questionText: Describe two methods of controlling crop pests and state one advantage of integrated pest management. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 98)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Methods include biological control, cultural practices, mechanical removal and appropriate pesticides. Integrated management combines suitable methods and can reduce over-reliance on chemicals.
questions.explanation: Methods and advantage should be correctly related.

questions.questionText: Explain the importance of keeping farm records. Name three records a farmer may keep. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 99)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Records help monitor production, costs, sales and profit and support planning. Examples include sales records, input records, livestock records and cash records.
questions.explanation: Any three valid record types.

questions.questionText: Describe three ways people can reduce environmental pollution in their community. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 100)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Proper waste disposal, recycling/reuse, treatment of sewage, reducing smoke emissions and planting trees can reduce pollution.
questions.explanation: Any three suitable measures with explanation.

questions.questionText: Explain two characteristics that show that an organism is living. Give one example of a living organism. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 101)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Living things grow, respire, reproduce, feed, excrete, respond to stimuli or move. Any two correctly explained characteristics earn credit.
questions.explanation: A characteristic is accepted when it is stated and appropriately explained.

questions.questionText: Describe the functions of the root, stem and leaf in a flowering plant. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 102)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water/mineral salts; the stem supports the plant and transports materials; leaves make food by photosynthesis and exchange gases.
questions.explanation: Functions should be matched to the correct plant parts.

questions.questionText: State two conditions necessary for successful seed germination and explain why each is needed. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 103)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Water is needed to activate processes and soften the seed coat; oxygen is needed for respiration; suitable warmth supports enzyme activity.
questions.explanation: Any two correct conditions with explanations are acceptable.

questions.questionText: Construct a simple four-organism food chain using a green plant, a herbivore, a carnivore and a decomposer. Explain the direction of energy flow. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 104)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Example: grass → grasshopper → frog → decomposer. Energy originates from the Sun, is captured by plants and passed through feeding relationships.
questions.explanation: Arrows should show feeding/energy transfer in the correct direction.

questions.questionText: Describe evaporation, condensation and precipitation as stages of the water cycle. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 105)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Evaporation changes liquid water to vapour; condensation changes vapour into tiny liquid droplets; precipitation returns water to Earth as rain or other forms.
questions.explanation: Each stage must be correctly described.

questions.questionText: Explain the main role of the respiratory system and describe how oxygen reaches the blood. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 106)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: The respiratory system brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide. In the lungs, oxygen passes from air spaces into the blood by gas exchange.
questions.explanation: The answer should link breathing, lungs and gas exchange.

questions.questionText: Give three ways of preventing the spread of infectious diseases in a community and explain each. Give detailed explanations and relevant examples where appropriate. (Practice item 107)
questions.correctAnswer: Model answer: Handwashing removes microbes; safe water and sanitation reduce contamination; vaccination can protect against specific diseases; covering coughs limits droplets.
questions.explanation: Any three appropriate measures with explanations.
